note.explanation: Biologists used observations, hypotheses, deductions and experiments to investigate malaria. Their evidence showed that Plasmodium causes malaria and that mosquitoes transmit it.
examples: Laveran found Plasmodium in the blood of a malarial patient.
Ross found that infected mosquitoes could transmit malaria to healthy sparrows.
note.checkAnswer: Ross found Plasmodium multiplying in mosquitoes and showed that infected mosquitoes transmitted malaria to healthy sparrows.
note.simple: Scientists noticed clues, made a possible explanation, and tested it. Their experiments showed that mosquitoes carry Plasmodium and can pass it on.
note.checkQuestion: What did Ross's experiments show about mosquitoes?
note.title: How scientists investigated malaria
steps: Make a deduction from the hypothesis.

note.answer: Mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium and are involved in the spread of malaria.

written.text: What is the role of observation and experimentation in the scientific method?
written.finalAnswer: Observations help identify a problem and suggest a hypothesis. Experiments test deductions made from the hypothesis and provide results to judge it.

rubric.why: Observation provides evidence and helps scientists identify a problem and form a hypothesis.
rubric.how: State that observations help identify the problem and suggest a hypothesis.

rubric.why: Experimentation tests the logical deduction and produces results.

written.text: How a hypothesis is converted to theory, law and principle?
written.finalAnswer: A hypothesis is tested by experiments. When an explanation is based on facts repeatedly confirmed through experiments, it becomes a scientific theory. If a theory is proved again and again by experiments, it becomes a law or principle. A scientific law is a uniform or constant fact of nature.

written.finalAnswer: A scientist recognizes a scientific problem, takes observations, makes a hypothesis, makes deductions, performs experiments, and summarizes and reports the results.

written.text: Describe the work of different scientists in discovering the cause of malaria.
written.finalAnswer: Laveran found Plasmodium in the blood of a malarial patient and suggested it was the cause of malaria. A. F. A. King proposed that mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium. Ronald Ross showed in sparrows that Plasmodium multiplies in mosquitoes and that infected mosquitoes transmit malaria. In 1898, Italian biologists confirmed mosquito transmission by allowing an infected Anopheles mosquito to bite a healthy man, who later developed malaria.

rubric.why: Laveran’s observation identified Plasmodium in malarial blood.
rubric.how: State that Laveran examined a malarial patient’s blood and found Plasmodium.

rubric.why: King’s hypothesis connected mosquitoes with the spread of malaria.
rubric.how: State that King suggested mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium.

rubric.why: Ross used sparrows to investigate mosquito transmission.
rubric.how: Mention Ross’s experiments using mosquitoes and sparrows.

rubric.why: The experiment showed Plasmodium’s development in the mosquito and transmission to sparrows.
rubric.how: Explain that Plasmodium multiplied in the mosquito and infected healthy sparrows.

rubric.why: The human experiment confirmed that mosquitoes transmit malaria to people.
rubric.how: Include the 1898 experiment in which an infected Anopheles bit a healthy man who later got malaria.

modelAnswer: In 1878, Laveran examined the blood of a malarial patient and noticed microorganisms, which were named Plasmodium.
Biologists suggested the hypothesis: “Plasmodium is the cause of malaria”.
A. F. A. King suggested the hypothesis: “Mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium and so are involved in the spread of malaria.”
Ronald Ross allowed female Culex mosquitoes to bite a sparrow suffering from malaria.
He found that Plasmodium multiplied in the walls of the mosquito’s stomach and then moved into its salivary glands.
He allowed infected mosquitoes to bite healthy sparrows, which got malaria.
In 1898, Italian biologists allowed an infected Anopheles mosquito to bite a healthy man, who later became ill with malaria.

written.text: Write a descriptive note on the experiments performed by Ross.
written.finalAnswer: Ross allowed a female Anopheles mosquito to bite a malarial patient. He killed it and found Plasmodium multiplying in its stomach. He then used sparrows instead of humans for the risky transmission experiment. Female Culex mosquitoes fed on an infected sparrow; Plasmodium multiplied in the walls of their stomachs and moved to their salivary glands. When infected mosquitoes bit healthy sparrows, the sparrows got malaria and Plasmodium was found in their blood. This showed that mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium.

rubric.why: This describes Ross’s first observation of Plasmodium in a mosquito.
rubric.how: State that a female Anopheles bit a malarial patient and Plasmodium was found in its stomach.

rubric.why: Ross used sparrows and Culex mosquitoes for the transmission experiment.
rubric.how: Name the sparrows and female Culex mosquitoes used.

rubric.why: The parasite’s movement within the mosquito supported the proposed transmission process.
rubric.how: Explain that Plasmodium multiplied in the stomach walls and moved into the salivary glands.

rubric.why: Illness in healthy sparrows demonstrated transmission.
rubric.how: State that healthy sparrows bitten by infected mosquitoes got malaria.

rubric.why: The final statement must give the conclusion supported by Ross’s experiments.
rubric.how: Conclude that mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium and are involved in spreading malaria.

modelAnswer: Ross allowed a female Anopheles mosquito to bite a malarial patient.
He killed this mosquito and found Plasmodium multiplying in its stomach.
Ross did not use human beings for the risky experiment, so he performed it again using sparrows.
He allowed female Culex mosquitoes to bite a sparrow suffering from malaria.
Plasmodium multiplied in the walls of the mosquito’s stomach and then moved into its salivary glands.
Ross allowed infected mosquitoes to bite healthy sparrows.
The healthy sparrows got malaria, and Ross found many Plasmodia in their blood.
This proved that mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium and are involved in the spread of malaria.

written.text: How can a scientist apply the scientific method to confirm an observation that a certain plant species grows more quickly in shady places than in direct sunlight?
written.finalAnswer: The scientist should recognize the problem and observe the plant’s growth in shady and sunny places. The hypothesis could be that the plant grows more quickly in shade. The deduction would be that, if this is true, plants of the same species grown in shade will show more growth than plants grown in direct sunlight over the same period. The scientist should grow comparable plants under both conditions while keeping other factors the same, measure their growth regularly, and compare the results. The results can then be summarized and reported to judge the hypothesis.

rubric.why: The investigation must begin with the stated observation and problem.
rubric.how: Identify the problem and compare growth in shady and sunny places.

rubric.why: A testable hypothesis gives a tentative explanation of the observation.
rubric.how: Propose that the plant grows more quickly in shade.

rubric.why: The deduction states an expected result if the hypothesis is true.
rubric.how: Predict greater growth in shade than in direct sunlight over the same period.

rubric.why: A fair experiment and measurements provide evidence for testing the deduction.
rubric.how: Compare similar plants in both conditions, keeping other factors the same and measuring growth.

rubric.why: The conclusion must use the results to judge the hypothesis.
rubric.how: Compare, summarize and report the results to decide whether the hypothesis is supported.

modelAnswer: Recognize the problem and observe the plant’s growth in shady and sunny places.
Hypothesis: The plant grows more quickly in shade.
Deduction: If the hypothesis is true, plants of the same species grown in shade will show more growth than plants grown in direct sunlight over the same period.
Grow comparable plants under both conditions, keeping other factors the same.
Measure the growth regularly and compare the results.
Summarize and report the results to judge the hypothesis.

steps.why: These observations gave biologists clues about the problem they were investigating.
steps.text: In the last part of 19th century, there were four major observations about malaria.

steps.why: Laveran’s observation identified a microorganism in the blood of a malaria patient.
steps.text: In 1878, a French army physician Laveran did research on the "cause of malaria".

steps.why: This finding led to the name Plasmodium and supported further investigation.
steps.text: He noticed some microorganisms in the blood. The microorganism was given a name – Plasmodium.

steps.why: A hypothesis is the proposed answer to the scientific problem.
steps.text: Biologists thought on these observations and discoveries and developed a hypothesis i.e. "Plasmodium is the cause of malaria"

steps.why: The deduction gives a result that should follow if the hypothesis is true.
steps.text: If Plasmodium is the cause of malaria, then all malarial patients should have Plasmodium in their blood.

steps.why: The experiment checked the predicted presence of Plasmodium in malaria patients and compared them with healthy people.
steps.text: They examined the blood samples of 100 malarial patients and 100 healthy persons under microscope.

steps.why: The result supported the hypothesis being tested.
steps.text: Most of the malarial patients had Plasmodium in their blood.

example.question: What is the cause of malaria?
example.answer: The experiments supported the hypothesis that Plasmodium is the cause of malaria.

explain.title: Hypothesis and deduction
explain.body: A hypothesis is a tentative answer to the scientific problem. A deduction is the logical result of the hypothesis. For example, if Plasmodium causes malaria, then it should be present in the blood of malarial patients.

explain.title: Testing the cause of malaria
explain.body: Biologists examined blood from 100 malarial patients and 100 healthy persons. The malarial patients were the experimental group, and the healthy persons were the control group. Most malarial patients had Plasmodium in their blood, supporting the hypothesis.

explain.title: Testing how malaria spreads
explain.body: King suggested that mosquitoes transmit Plasmodium. Ross found Plasmodium in mosquitoes and used infected mosquitoes to infect healthy sparrows. Later, Italian biologists confirmed transmission to humans using Anopheles mosquitoes.

explain.title: Scientific method
explain.body: The scientific method involves basic steps like recognition of scientific problem, taking observations, making hypothesis, making deductions, performing experiments and summarizing and reporting results.

explain.title: Theory and law
explain.body: A scientific theory is an explanation based on the facts that have been repeatedly confirmed through experiments. If a theory is proved again and again by experiments, it becomes a law or principle. A scientific law is a uniform or constant fact of nature.

mistakes: Do not mix up a hypothesis with a deduction: the hypothesis is a tentative answer, while the deduction is its logical prediction.
Do not call the healthy persons the experimental group; they were the control group.
Do not say Ross used humans for his risky experiment. He used sparrows, and Italian biologists later performed the human experiment.
Do not leave out the result of an experiment. State what was found and what it showed.
Use the correct mosquito names: Ross used Culex with sparrows; the human malaria experiments used Anopheles.
